question: The income of Raman is ₹43,500. He saves 17% of his income. If his income increases by 18% and expenditure increases by 20%, then his savings will:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Income = 43500, Savings = 17% → Expenditure = 83%

New income = 43500 × 1.18, New expenditure = 83% × 1.20

Net saving % = 118% − (83 × 1.20)% = 118 − 99.6 = 18.4%

Increase in saving % = 18.4 − 17 = 1.4%

**∴ Savings increase by 1.4% of original income = 609**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Income = 43500, Savings = 17%

**Formula used:**

Savings = Income − Expenditure

**Calculation:**

⇒ Initial savings = 17% of 43500 = 7395

⇒ Initial expenditure = 43500 − 7395 = 36105

⇒ New income = 43500 × 1.18 = 51330

⇒ New expenditure = 36105 × 1.20 = 43326

⇒ New savings = 51330 − 43326 = 8004

⇒ Increase in savings = 8004 − 7395 = 609

**∴ The savings increase by ₹609.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Income–Expenditure Relation

Savings = Income − Expenditure

Percentage Increase

New value = Original × (1 + % increase)

Saving Percentage Trick

If savings = x%, expenditure = (100 − x)%

Combined Effect

Always adjust both income and expenditure separately before subtracting.
